candidates.title: Life After Death | Evolution Series 72
candidates.speaker: Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji
candidates.topic: Death as a sacred transition in an unending stream of consciousness
candidates.verbatim_quote: If you looked at the perception of life as an unending stream of consciousness without birth, without death, your current experience of life itself becomes very sacred. The people you meet in your life, you know are people with whom you have shared lifetimes of connection. That you know you have a shared journey, a shared mission to accomplish on this planet. You have a shared evolution to achieve in this lifetime. This brings a greater significance to human relationship itself. You are not terrified of death or old age because you know you have been old many times before and that death is only a transition from one phase to another.
candidates.clinical_safeguard_notes: Screens clean against _CLIP_MENTIONS_SELF_HARM. Provides spiritual perspective on mortality, honoring connections across lifetimes, without morbid ideation.

candidates.title: Life After Death | Evolution Series 72
candidates.speaker: Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji
candidates.topic: Releasing departed ancestors into light and experiencing emotional liberation
candidates.verbatim_quote: One of the gifts that is offered is releasing the departed. Thousands today have a first-hand experience of releasing the departed. They experience an instant liberation and instant emotional release when their departed move into the light in a state of peace. Long-standing obstacles give way and the dissolution of health problems happens in the family when the departed move into the light. It is a stuck energy and a restless energy that has been cleared.
candidates.clinical_safeguard_notes: Addresses feelings of stuck emotional grief and unresolved guilt regarding departed loved ones. Offers positive psychological release and familial healing.

candidates.title: Life After Death | Evolution Series 72
candidates.speaker: Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji
candidates.category: Fearlessness in the Face of Mortality
candidates.topic: Mahaprasthana: Living fully without regret and loving completely without reserve
candidates.verbatim_quote: That is why death is called Mahaprasthana, which means the commencement of a great journey. Life and afterlife are fundamentally like dreams you wake up from and come into waking. Only which of this is waking and which of this is the dreaming is the question. The only way you can be fearless about death is when you live life fully without regret. The only way you will be ready to embrace death when it comes knocking is when you love completely without reserve.
candidates.clinical_safeguard_notes: Inspirational spiritual discourse redirecting sorrow toward unconditional love and present living.

candidates.title: How to know when it's time to let go
candidates.speaker: Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji
candidates.topic: Awakening a grander state of consciousness when facing the death of a parent or loss of love
candidates.verbatim_quote: When disaster occurs or when life slowly and gradually turns bitter and disappointing, because of the death of a parent, the loss of love, the gradual dissolution of a dream, we experience the same suffering that humans have endured since the beginning of time. But despite all our technological advancements, modern society has not given us the tools we need to emerge from these crisis with a grander state of consciousness we need for the next chapter.
candidates.clinical_safeguard_notes: Directly names the death of a parent and loss of love, framing the pain as universal human experience and orienting the seeker toward inner growth and resilience.

candidates.title: Spiritual hacks to heal heartache and depression
candidates.speaker: Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji
candidates.topic: Physical presence, connection, and sending healing love to relieve heartache
candidates.verbatim_quote: Gentle and loving physical touch while you actually hold an intention for the other to be happy can actually relieve a heartache and heal the other. A healing love flows from your body to the other when you are in a Beautiful State of love and hold a heartfelt wish for the well-being of the other. Your body actually emanates healing influence on the other.
candidates.clinical_safeguard_notes: Practical relational guidance for supporters or seekers experiencing emotional heartbreak or grief.

candidates.title: How to become free of sorrow flowing from the past
candidates.speaker: Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji
candidates.category: Freedom from Generational and Chronic Sorrow
candidates.topic: Recognizing sorrow that flows through memories and ancestry, and freeing oneself from it
candidates.verbatim_quote: So, the past is a part of you - the good things of the past, the bad things of the past. But for some reason, if you are constantly feeling sorrow or sadness, then it need not be from the past that's happening to you, from this life. Your past is just not from the time you were born. Your past moves beyond that... Now, is it possible to become free of that sorrow that is flowing from the past? We don't know from where it's exactly flowing, but from wherever it is flowing, is it possible to become free of it? The answer is yes. It is possible to become free of this past today.
candidates.clinical_safeguard_notes: Validates chronic sorrow while giving hope and affirmation of liberation without despair.

candidates.title: Awakening to Compassion and the Oneness of Human Experience
candidates.speaker: Sri Preethaji & Sri Krishnaji
candidates.topic: Recognizing that human sorrow is shared, dissolving isolation in times of pain
candidates.verbatim_quote: My experience of fear and your experience of fear is not different. It is not separate. My experience of sorrow and your experience of sorrow is just the same. If we move away from holding on to the superficial differences that we experience and move into the oneness of human experience, then we will awaken to compassion.
candidates.clinical_safeguard_notes: Counteracts the profound isolation felt during grief by highlighting universal human connection.
